lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The file includes personal details that a reader is not meant to weigh.
items.because: Date of birth and nationality do not establish finance qualifications and draw attention away from work experience and results.

items.says: The experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: Crescent Bank appears above the more recent Stonebridge Manufacturing role.

items.says: Education leads the page instead of the five years of work experience.
items.because: The degree appears before the roles showing more recent finance work.

items.says: The Student Investment Fund entry takes more space than its relevance warrants.
The résumé does not show employment after June 2025.
items.because: The only activity shown after that is the ongoing independent valuation project.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration does not hedge the existing holdings’ interest-rate risk.
items.because: The additional bonds generally move in the same direction as the existing holdings, increasing exposure without an offsetting position.

items.says: The claimed interest-rate hedge has no measure of how much risk changed.
The description of fixed-rate bonds is repeated unnecessarily.
“My findings” does not reveal what the review found in declined applications.
items.because: The reader cannot see the analytical insight connecting the review to the threshold changes.

items.says: The strongest Crescent Bank bullet is not first.
items.because: Placing it after the bond claim delays evidence of the candidate’s credit-analysis work.

items.says: “No rise in early defaults” omits the period over which defaults were observed.
“My findings” introduces a personal pronoun into the bullet.
“Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in 2022.
The bullet says it cut each memo rather than the time spent preparing one.
“Monthly forecast error under 4%” does not identify the cash-flow measure or measurement period.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret the accuracy without knowing what the forecasts were compared with and when.

items.says: The forecast bullet names the deliverable but not its modeling approach.
The close bullet does not show what automation the candidate implemented.
The capital-plan bullet states its standardization result wordily.
The journal-entry reduction is buried after a long list of methods.
items.because: A reader must get through the methods before reaching the reduction from 350 to 90 entries a month.

items.says: Discounting free cash flow to equity at weighted average cost of capital mismatches the cash flow and discount rate.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity calls for a cost of equity; WACC belongs with cash flow available to both debt and equity providers.

items.says: The acquisition-target bullet does not say how the valuation was used.
The training bullet does not state what the training and guide enabled or changed.
The market-price comparison does not state what the valuation concluded for an investor.
“Landing within 6% of the market price” is a casual, wordy description of the result.
The fall from USD 50 to USD 40 is a 20% drop, not a 25% drop.
items.because: The USD 10 decrease is measured against the starting USD 50 value.

items.says: “1 point” does not specify the unit of the discount-rate increase.
The increase from 70% to 82% is 12 percentage points, not 12%.
items.because: Calling it 12% confuses the percentage-point change with the approximately 17.1% relative increase.

items.says: The accuracy claim does not identify what was forecast, what it was checked against, or what “across 10 years” measures.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret the accuracy figures or tell whether 10 years is the forecast horizon or assessment period.

items.says: “Supported the FP&A team” does not identify an output or result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the candidate produced or what need the contribution served.

items.says: “Financial reporting and analysis” does not show which task the candidate performed.
items.because: The phrase names an area of work rather than an action.

items.says: The strongest Student Investment Fund bullet is not first.
items.because: Opening with the broad support claim delays the clearest evidence of the candidate’s contribution.

items.says: “On the fund’s models” leaves the subject of the onboarding notes too broad.
“For new analysts” names the audience but not what the notes enabled them to do.
